title: iPad (11th gen) speaker replacement
diagnosis: No sound is most likely a failed speaker box or a loose connection, though a software mute can look the same. We'll rule out the simple causes first, then open the iPad and check or replace the speakers. This is a hard repair because the display is glued on and has to be heated off.
safety_notes: Power off the iPad and unplug the charger before opening it.
Do not puncture or bend the battery cells; keep the spudger away from them.
Disconnect the battery flex before touching any other connector.
Never use a metal tool to pry near the battery.

steps.title: Power off and rule out software
steps.instruction: Unplug all cables and remove any case. Check the mute switch or Control Center, test with headphones, then hold the top button and slide to power off.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad screen is black, with no cables attached and no case on it.
common_mistakes: Skipping the software check and opening the iPad when the sound was just muted
Leaving the charger plugged in

steps.title: Heat and lift the display
steps.instruction: Warm the edges of the screen with a hair dryer until it is hot to the touch. Attach the suction handle and slide an opening pick into the small gap.
steps.expected_visual_state: A thin gap is visible along one edge of the display, with an opening pick inserted in it.
common_mistakes: Not heating long enough, so the glass cracks when pulled
Inserting the pick deeper than a few millimetres and damaging the flexes
Overheating one spot

steps.title: Release the display adhesive
steps.instruction: Slide picks around all the edges to cut the adhesive. Lift the display slowly like a book, resting it on its side.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display is lifted and propped open, with the display flexes still attached and the inside of the iPad visible.
common_mistakes: Yanking the display open and tearing the flexes
Cutting too deeply near the battery cells

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Unscrew the display cable bracket with the P2 Phillips screwdriver. Then pry the battery flex connector straight up with a plastic spudger.
steps.expected_visual_state: The bracket is removed with its screws set aside in a row, and the battery connector is lifted clear of its socket.
common_mistakes: Losing the tiny screws
Prying the connector at an angle and bending its pins
Skipping this step and working on a live board

steps.title: Inspect the speakers and connections
steps.instruction: Look at the four speaker boxes along the top and bottom edges for loose, damaged or dirty contacts. Press each speaker connection gently to reseat it.
steps.expected_visual_state: The speaker boxes are visible, with their contacts clean and seated against the board.
common_mistakes: Pulling on the speaker flexes
Touching the speaker cones with a tool

steps.title: Swap the faulty speaker
steps.instruction: Remove the speaker screws and lift the dead speaker out with tweezers. Fit the new speaker in the same spot and tighten the screws.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new speaker sits flush in its recess, fixed with all screws, with the old speaker removed.
common_mistakes: Mixing up top and bottom speakers
Over-tightening the small screws
Leaving the foam or gasket out

steps.title: Reconnect and test before closing
steps.instruction: Reconnect the battery flex and refit the display bracket. Rest the display on the iPad, power on and play a sound.
steps.expected_visual_state: The iPad powers on and shows the Apple logo, and audio is audible with the volume up.
common_mistakes: Pressing the battery connector in crooked
Forgetting the display bracket
Closing the iPad before testing

steps.title: Seal the display and run a final test
steps.instruction: Power off, then press the display down along all edges until it sticks. Power on and play music at several volumes to confirm every speaker works.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display sits flat in the shell with even edges, and sound plays clearly from the speaker grilles.
common_mistakes: Leaving gaps along the edge
Not pressing the corners down firmly
Testing only one speaker
